newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate steady as finance firms borrow.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate steady as finance firms borrow.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was steady on Wednesday on bids by finance commpanies seeking fresh funds, dealers said.
The overnight traded between 8.5 and 8.9 percent against 8.5/9.0 percent on Tuesday.
Dealers said a shortage of funds at the short-end of the market continued to boost rates.
"It's still quite tight and there are not many lenders," said a Malaysian bank dealer.
"Unless banks are really short, I don't think there will be much borrowing. It's so expensive to borrow at current levels," he said.
Dealers said they expected rates to remain high until new funds flow in.
The current tightness was caused by a mismatch of funds, with foreign banks holding a lot of funds while local banks were short, dealers said.
Earlier, one-week money was traded at 8.80 percent, two-week at 8.90 percent and three-week at 8.70 percent. They were at 8.0/8.50 percent on Tuesday.
The one-month rate was at 8.30 percent against 8.0/8.20, while three-month money was steady at 8.0/8.10 percent.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange fell across the board, extending their bearish tone in view of the tight cash market, futures dealers said.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down 15 points to 92.19, or an implied yield of 7.81 percent.
September contract fell 11 to 92.40, or 7.60 percent and December was down seven to 92.51, or 7.49.
